questions.question_text: A clean iron nail is placed in copper sulphate solution. Which observation is expected after some time?
questions.option_a: The blue solution becomes pale green and copper deposits on the nail
questions.option_b: The solution becomes colourless and oxygen bubbles form
questions.option_c: The nail dissolves without any colour change
questions.option_d: The solution turns deep blue and zinc deposits on the nail
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces Cu²⁺; FeSO₄ is pale green and copper is deposited.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which metal can displace iron from iron(II) sulphate solution but cannot displace magnesium from magnesium sulphate?
questions.explanation: Zinc lies above iron but below magnesium in the reactivity series, so it displaces iron but not magnesium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does aluminium often resist further corrosion despite being a reactive metal?
questions.option_a: It is below gold in the reactivity series
questions.option_b: It forms a thin, adherent oxide layer that limits further attack
questions.option_c: It does not react with oxygen
questions.explanation: The compact Al₂O₃ film passivates the surface and protects underlying aluminium from continued oxidation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A metal is extracted from its oxide by heating the oxide with carbon. Which conclusion about the metal is most justified?
questions.option_a: It is generally less reactive than carbon
questions.option_b: It must be more reactive than potassium
questions.option_c: It is necessarily a noble metal
questions.explanation: Carbon can reduce oxides of metals below it in the reactivity series; highly reactive metals require other extraction methods.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair correctly matches a sulphide ore with the usual first step in its conversion to oxide?
questions.explanation: Sulphide ores such as ZnS are commonly roasted in excess air to form the oxide and sulphur dioxide.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A carbonate ore is heated strongly in limited or no air before reduction. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Calcination thermally decomposes carbonate or hydrated ores, generally with limited air, to produce an oxide.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During electrolytic refining of copper, where does the impure copper undergo oxidation and dissolve?
questions.option_d: On the outer surface of the electrolyte
questions.explanation: The impure metal is the anode; copper ions enter solution and purer copper is deposited at the cathode.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In an electrolytic cell used to extract a highly reactive metal, where is the metal generally produced?
questions.option_a: At the anode by oxidation of the metal ion
questions.option_b: At the cathode by reduction of the metal ion
questions.explanation: Metal cations gain electrons at the cathode. Electrolysis is used for metals too reactive for carbon reduction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is sodium stored under kerosene?
questions.option_a: To prevent it from reacting vigorously with oxygen and moisture
questions.option_b: To keep it molten at room temperature
questions.option_c: To convert it into sodium hydroxide slowly
questions.option_d: Because sodium dissolves in kerosene to form an alloy
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts vigorously with oxygen and water; an oil layer limits contact with air and moisture.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A metal reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and releases a gas that burns with a characteristic pop. Which ion is reduced in this reaction?
questions.explanation: The metal is oxidised while H⁺ ions gain electrons to form hydrogen gas.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which metal is least likely to liberate hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid under ordinary conditions?
questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the usual reactivity series and does not displace hydrogen from dilute non-oxidising acids.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An iron object is coated with zinc to protect it from rusting. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Galvanisation applies a zinc coating; zinc also offers sacrificial protection if the coating is scratched.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A small scratch exposes iron beneath a zinc coating. Why can the zinc still protect the iron sacrificially?
questions.option_a: Zinc is less reactive and blocks every electron transfer
questions.option_c: Zinc converts iron into stainless steel
questions.option_d: Zinc removes oxygen from water permanently
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron and corrodes preferentially, delaying oxidation of the exposed iron.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement best explains why solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity but molten sodium chloride does?
questions.option_b: Its ions are fixed in the solid lattice but mobile when molten
questions.option_c: Molten NaCl contains free electrons only
questions.option_d: Heating converts sodium ions into neutral atoms
questions.explanation: Ions are present in both states, but only in the molten state can they move and carry electric charge.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Ionic compounds commonly have high melting points because their crystal lattice contains
questions.option_b: strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions
questions.option_c: only covalent bonds between metal atoms
questions.option_d: mobile electrons that repel every ion
questions.explanation: Considerable energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic forces holding oppositely charged ions in the lattice.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Aluminium oxide reacts with both hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide. What classification does this support?
questions.explanation: An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases is classified as amphoteric; Al₂O₃ is a standard example.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which observation is evidence that aluminium oxide is amphoteric?
questions.option_a: It reacts with both an acid and a base
questions.option_c: It conducts electricity as a solid
questions.explanation: Amphoteric oxides show both acidic and basic behaviour by reacting with bases as well as acids.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which metal is obtained from bauxite on a large industrial scale by electrolytic reduction rather than reduction with carbon?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is highly reactive; its extraction from alumina uses electrolysis rather than carbon reduction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The thermite reaction uses aluminium powder to reduce iron(III) oxide. Aluminium acts as the
questions.option_a: oxidising agent because it gains oxygen
questions.option_b: reducing agent because it removes oxygen from iron oxide
questions.option_d: acid because it releases hydrogen ions
questions.explanation: Aluminium is oxidised to aluminium oxide while reducing iron oxide to molten iron, so it is the reducing agent.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which alloy is principally made from copper and zinc?
questions.explanation: Brass is mainly copper and zinc; bronze is mainly copper and tin.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which two metals are the principal constituents of nichrome, the alloy commonly used in heating elements?
questions.explanation: Nichrome is a nickel–chromium alloy, valued for high resistivity and resistance to oxidation at elevated temperatures.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why are pure metals often alloyed for engineering uses?
questions.option_a: To make them chemically identical to noble gases
questions.option_b: To modify properties such as hardness, strength or corrosion resistance
questions.option_c: To ensure they melt at exactly 0 °C
questions.explanation: Alloying alters a metal's properties; many alloys are harder or more corrosion-resistant than the constituent pure metals.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A metal forms a brittle solid oxide when burned in oxygen. Which broad chemical behaviour is most expected when that oxide is treated with an acid?
questions.option_a: It may form a salt and water if the oxide is basic
questions.option_c: It can only form an alloy
questions.explanation: A basic metal oxide commonly neutralises an acid to produce a salt and water; the exact reaction depends on the oxide.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which non-metal is commonly used in vulcanisation of rubber, illustrating a practical use of a non-metallic element?
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links between rubber polymer chains during vulcanisation, improving useful mechanical properties.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair consists of metals that are liquid near ordinary room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is liquid at ordinary room temperature; gallium melts just above typical room temperature and may liquefy in a warm hand. The other listed element pairs include non-metals or solids.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement distinguishes roasting from calcination in common ore processing?
questions.option_a: Roasting heats mainly sulphide ores in air; calcination heats carbonate or hydrated ores with limited air
questions.option_b: Roasting is electrolysis; calcination is filtration
questions.option_c: Roasting applies only to native metals; calcination only to alloys
questions.option_d: The two terms always describe identical conditions
questions.explanation: Roasting is typically used for sulphide ores in excess air, whereas calcination decomposes carbonate or hydrated ores with little or no air.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A strip of copper is placed in silver nitrate solution. Which change is consistent with the reactivity series?
questions.option_a: Silver deposits on copper while copper enters solution as ions
questions.option_b: Copper deposits on silver while nitrate gas escapes
questions.option_c: No reaction because silver is more reactive than copper
questions.option_d: The solution becomes alkaline and hydrogen is released
questions.explanation: Copper is more reactive than silver and displaces silver ions, depositing silver and forming copper(II) nitrate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about displacement reactions is correct?
questions.option_a: A less reactive metal displaces a more reactive metal from its salt
questions.option_b: A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution
questions.option_d: The order of reactivity is irrelevant
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal can replace a less reactive metal from its compound, as in iron displacing copper from copper sulphate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which material is commonly used as the sacrificial anode to protect a ship's iron hull from corrosion?
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal such as zinc or magnesium corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron hull cathodically.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The reddish-brown flaky product formed when iron corrodes in moist air is best described as
questions.option_b: hydrated iron(III) oxide of variable composition
questions.explanation: Rust is commonly described as hydrated iron(III) oxide; its water content and exact composition vary.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Metals and Non-metals, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
